Team — thanks for a focused weekly sync this morning. I know we ran long, so below is a concise capture of the asks and owners I promised to circulate. Please reply only if anything below is incorrect or if you need the deadline adjusted.

Summary (top-level):
- Exec asks: finalize the exception list we will present at the QBR deck by end of day Thursday (3/31).
- Roadmap exceptions: confirm whether the model quantization milestone can slip to M2 or must remain in M1.
- SLA edge-case: determine if the dedicated fallback behavior requires a policy change (owner: Vivek).

Action items (owners & due dates):
1) Marcus — annotate the exceptions_matrix.xlsx with impact (latency, cost, customer risk) and mark any "must-fix" items by 2027-03-31 EOD. Attachment: exceptions_matrix.xlsx.
2) Vivek — provide a one-paragraph proposal for fallback routing and whether we need an SLA carve-out (due 2027-03-31 17:00 PDT).
3) Laura — draft 1 slide for QBR that summarizes exceptions + proposed remediation timeline (due 2027-03-31 12:00 PDT). Use the shared doc link below for slide notes.
4) Jasmine (me) — consolidate final deck + send to Execs by 2027-03-31 18:00 PDT.

Notes/constraints discussed:
- We can use temporary canary capacity for the highest-risk customer but that is a short-term mitigation only.
- Priya from TerraCloud joined for context; their request to accelerate the quantization timeline is noted but does not change internal prioritization today.

Related links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2B_exceptions_playbook

Thanks — please keep updates short (one-line) so I can roll them into the deck.

--
Jasmine Liu
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni To: Jasmine Liu , Laura Bennett , Marcus Lin Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -0700 Subject: Re: Actions from cross-functional sync (exceptions, exec asks, QBR prep) Thanks, Jasmine — catching up quickly. Two clarifications and a quick note on feasibility: 1) SLA fallback proposal: I will outline a 3-tier fallback: same-region model variant, cross-region (latency-impacting), and reserved-burst for top-tier customers. The decision point: do we want automatic cross-region fallback at a cost threshold or keep it manual? I recommend automatic for P1 customers only. 2) Quantization timeline: from infra's perspective, M1 can ship a prototype for internal testing by M1 end, but production readiness requires additional QA that likely pushes full rollout into M2 unless we accept a 10–15% quality delta. Marcus — would like your risk assessment in the matrix to confirm. I'll attach a one-paragraph proposal to my follow-up (short PDF) and tag the policy decision points.
